summary.headline: NOCIL H1 FY27 revenue rose 26% to Rs.830 crore on higher prices; Q2 volumes fell 3% YoY on supply and logistics constraints, and FY27 guided to upper end of Rs.1,400-1,600 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs.427 crore, up 33% YoY and 6% QoQ, driven mainly by higher average selling prices, while volumes fell 3% YoY and 7% QoQ due to temporary supply-side and logistics constraints linked to the geopolitical situation. Q2 EBITDA was Rs.36 crore (8.4% margin), up 61% YoY but down 20% QoQ; PAT was Rs.24 crore, up 98% YoY and down 13% QoQ. Management says the supply issues are now addressed, expects volumes to recover in H2, and remains confident of FY27 revenue at the upper end of Rs.1,400-1,600 crore with EBITDA margin around 10%. Import dumping and higher utility, coal, gas and freight costs weighed on the quarter.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic volumes grew at a single-digit rate in H1 FY27, aided by demand after GST 2.0 implementation.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export volumes grew at a single-digit rate in H1 FY27; management expects international opportunities to convert and contribute to H2 volume growth, with specialty rubber chemicals in similar ratios.

segments.name: Antioxidants
segments.commentary: Management said antioxidants are about 60% of the business; sulfonamides ADD is a small portion of the basket.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected towards the upper end of the Rs.1,400-1,600 crore range; management said current pricing could exceed Rs.1,600 crore but it is staying conservative.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at around 10%.
H2 FY27 volume growth expected at 8-10% for the full year, implying an index of about 160-165 in H2; management said this growth is a fair base for FY28 as well.
Q3 FY27 realisations seen with a marginal uptick versus H1 at current prices.
Gross profit run rate of about Rs.700 crore annualised cited versus about Rs.520-525 crore a year earlier; conversion cost run rate about Rs.520 crore per analyst math.
TDQ capitalisation expected in Q3 FY27 once pending customer approvals are received; annual depreciation on the Rs.220 crore base expected to rise by about Rs.3 crore per quarter.
capex_capacity: Brownfield TDQ expansion at Dahej has delivered ahead of schedule and is progressing towards customer approvals expected over coming months.
Integrated specialty rubber chemicals project progressing as planned.
Board-sanctioned Rs.130 crore spend, partly done, to be split between H2 FY27 and H1 FY28, plus routine maintenance capex; no other major capex foreseen.
Captive power boilers and turbines expected to contribute as volumes ramp in H2 FY27; power issues from Q1 described as addressed.
Management is exploring inorganic growth opportunities in the chemical space; no development announced.
demand_pricing: Q2 volumes were held back by temporary supply-side constraints and logistics issues tied to the geopolitical situation; management says customer engagement and underlying demand remain healthy.

Domestic tyre demand supported by GST 2.0 consumption, but a weaker monsoon, inflation and some tyre-volume downgrades by rating agencies (from 8% to 4-5%, as cited by an analyst) are near-term headwinds.
Competitive pressure from imports, including import dumping; management aims to balance price and volume.
Realisations rose about Rs.100 per kg YoY per an analyst; management said ADD on sulfonamides contributed only a small, unquantified part.
Conversion costs rose by about Rs.10-20 per kg per an analyst, driven by coal and gas prices, domestic and sea freight; management expects H2 operating leverage to offset part of this.
No significant new Chinese capacity additions beyond those already announced, per management.
Antidumping duty on 4ADPA (precursor to PILFLEX-13) was not notified or accepted by the government; the effect on domestic peers would be indirect and uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of H2 volume growth, given FY27 assumptions imply an index of about 165, and does this carry into FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 8-10% volume growth for the year, with H2 index at least 160-165, coming from both domestic and international markets; it agreed 10% is a fair FY28 assumption.

qa_highlights.question: Is the revenue and margin guidance conservative given run-rate math implying about Rs.180 crore EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged some conservatism given the evolving environment, but said it will strive to achieve more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for conversion costs, which rose by Rs.10-20 per kg as freight and power benefits faded?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher coal and gas costs and sea freight drove the increase; management expects H2 leverage from higher volumes to help once supply constraints are cleared.

qa_highlights.question: How much additional margin can ADD on 4ADPA provide, and what is the sulfonamides benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: 4ADPA duty on PILFLEX-13 precursor was not notified; the impact on domestic peers is indirect. Sulfonamides import data is unavailable, so the benefit cannot be quantified, though some is factored into pricing.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the realisation increase comes from ADD versus cost pass-through, and is the steady-state margin weakening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ADD is only on sulfonamides, a small portion of the business; the price increase mainly reflects cost pass-through, plus an improved value-add shift this year, with the ADD share not quantifiable.

qa_highlights.question: How much inventory risk is there from input-price reversal, and when will TDQ be capitalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital has fallen to about 25% of sales; inventory is held for roughly 40-60 days with no significant near-term effect. TDQ capitalisation awaits customer approvals, hoped for in Q3, adding about Rs.3 crore depreciation per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gross profit per tonne sustained, and how much is ADD versus market conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ADD was part of Q2 gross margin but not all of it; market conditions improved versus last year, with the gross profit run rate up from about Rs.520-525 crore to Rs.700 crore a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the implied H2 realisation and capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current pricing shows a marginal uptick in Q3 versus H1; the Rs.130 crore Board-sanctioned capex will be spent across H2 FY27 and H1 FY28 alongside maintenance capex.

risks_watch: H2 volume ramp of 16% (index 160-165) is required to meet guidance; delivery depends on clearing supply and logistics constraints.
Inventory reversal risk if input prices fall; prices dipped between Q1 and Q2 before rising again.
Sustainability of the margin uplift if ADD benefits fade, since ADD on sulfonamides is small and unquantified.
TDQ capitalisation and return without ADD protection depend on pending customer approvals.
Rising coal, gas, freight and conversion costs, plus weaker monsoon and inflation effects on tyre demand.
Import competition, and potential new capacity from China.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously confident: management is positive on the medium-term outlook and H2 volume recovery, but repeatedly flagged near-term challenges from geopolitics, input costs and competition. It was evasive on quantifying ADD benefits and the drivers of the Q2 margin.
key_quotes: We, therefore, remain positive on the industry's long-term prospects, while recognizing that the near-term operating environment continues to be challenging.
We have addressed the supply side constraints, and we expect the affected volumes to recover in the second half.
Given our H1 performance and the current momentum, we remain confident of closing FY27 towards the upper end of this range with EBITDA margins of around 10%.

adds.what: Brownfield TDQ expansion at Dahej (capitalisation pending customer approvals)
Integrated specialty rubber chemicals project (progressing as planned, no size or timing given)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided to upper end of Rs.1,400-1,600 crore with ~10% EBITDA margin and 8-10% FY27 volume growth, backed partly by Dahej TDQ capacity (Rs.130 crore spend, capitalisation expected Q3 FY27 pending customer approvals) and H2 volume recovery, though no firm order or capacity numbers were given for the volume ramp.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided around 10% versus H1 at 9.8% and Q2 at 8.4%, with H2 operating leverage expected, but conversion costs rose Rs.10-20/kg and ADD benefit is small and unquantified.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Dahej TDQ brownfield expansion (Rs.130 crore) has delivered ahead of schedule and is expected to be capitalised in Q3 FY27 once customer approvals arrive, adding about Rs.3 crore depreciation per quarter; approvals are not yet confirmed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 8-10% FY27 volume growth, requiring H2 index of about 160-165 versus Q2 at 135 (down 3% YoY, 7% QoQ), and calls 10% a fair FY28 base, but supply and logistics constraints must clear first.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Board-sanctioned Rs.130 crore spend is being deployed across H2 FY27 and H1 FY28 with no other major capex foreseen, and management is exploring inorganic opportunities without any announcement, so a fresh capex is possible rather than likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says current pricing could exceed Rs.1,600 crore against guidance of Rs.1,400-1,600 crore, and acknowledged some conservatism, but it is staying cautious given geopolitics and input costs.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 needs a 16% volume ramp to hit guidance, while Q2 EBITDA fell 20% QoQ, conversion costs rose Rs.10-20/kg, and import dumping and weaker monsoon demand are headwinds.

rows.label: Export order conversion for H2 volume
rows.why: Management expects international opportunities to convert and add to H2 volume growth, but export volumes grew only at a single-digit rate in H1 FY27.

rows.label: Working capital release to about 25% of sales
rows.why: Working capital has fallen to about 25% of sales from about 30-32% in March 2025, though a reversal in input prices could create inventory risk.

rows.label: Marginal Q3 realisation uptick
rows.why: Management sees Q3 realisations marginally up versus H1 at current prices, with the gross profit run rate at about Rs.700 crore annualised versus Rs.520-525 crore a year earlier.

tone.note: Management was confident on the medium-term outlook, H2 volume recovery, and FY27 guidance, but cautious on geopolitics, input costs and import competition; analysts pressed on the run-rate implied EBITDA, ADD contribution to margins, and the H2 volume ramp, and management was evasive on quantifying
